Convert a detection array to the long format of mvgam

Source: R/data_helpers.R
pivot_detection_array.Rd

Occupancy and N-mixture packages such as unmarked, ubms, flocker and spOccupancy store detection histories as matrices or arrays, with one dimension for sites and one for visits. mvgam() and jsdgam() with occ() or nmix() take a long data frame instead, with one row per species, site, season and visit. This function converts the one to the other and copies the covariates onto the matching rows.

Data from one season give time = site. Each site is then one closure unit. Data from several seasons take one of two layouts, chosen by multi_season:

  • "fused" (the default) gives each site in each season its own closure unit, with time = (site - 1) * T + season for \(T\) seasons. Use it when the seasons are independent given the covariates.

  • "hierarchical" keeps time = season. Fit it with occ(multi_season = TRUE) or nmix(multi_season = TRUE). Name site in the observation formula, as in s(site, bs = "re"). The latent trend then runs over seasons. The model has no explicit colonisation or extinction rates.

Usage

pivot_detection_array(
  y,
  site_covs = NULL,
  season_covs = NULL,
  site_season_covs = NULL,
  obs_covs = NULL,
  species = NULL,
  site_col = "site",
  season_col = "season",
  visit_col = "visit",
  time_col = "time",
  series_col = "series",
  y_col = "y",
  multi_season = c("fused", "hierarchical")
)

Arguments

y

One of four layouts:

  • Single-species, single-season: a [J_sites, K_max_visits] matrix of detections (0 / 1 for occ(), non-negative counts for nmix()). The unmarked::unmarkedFrameOccu / unmarkedFramePCount y slot and the flocker::flock obs argument with type = "single".

  • Multi-species, single-season (array): a [N_species, J_sites, K_max_visits] array. The spOccupancy::lfMsPGOcc / msPGOcc y slot.

  • Multi-species, single-season (list): a named list of [J_sites, K_max_visits] matrices, one per species. The unmarked::unmarkedFrameOccuMulti y slot; list names become species labels.

  • Multi-species, multi-season: a [N_species, J_sites, T_seasons, K_max_visits] 4D array. The spOccupancy::tMsPGOcc / svcTMsPGOcc y slot. For single-species multi-season data, wrap in a length-1 list (list(only_species = matrix_or_3d_array)) or pass as a [1, J, T, K] array.

NA entries mark missing visits / seasons and are dropped from the output.

site_covs

Optional data.frame of site-level covariates with nrow == J_sites. Broadcast across visits, seasons and species. The unmarked::unmarkedFrameOccu siteCovs slot, the spOccupancy occ.covs and the flocker unit_covs map here.

season_covs

Optional data.frame of season-level covariates with nrow == T_seasons. Broadcast across sites, visits and species. Use for year-of-study effects, season-of-year covariates, or any covariate that varies across primary periods but is constant within a season.

site_season_covs

Optional named list of [J_sites, T_seasons] matrices for covariates that vary across the (site, season) interaction (e.g., site-level habitat that changes between seasons).

obs_covs

Optional visit-level covariates:

  • Single-season: named list of [J_sites, K_max_visits] matrices, OR a long-format data.frame with J_sites * K_max_visits rows in site-major / visit-fastest order (the unmarked obsCovs convention).

  • Multi-season: named list of [J_sites, T_seasons, K_max_visits] arrays.

species

Optional character vector of species names with length == N_species. Only meaningful for multi-species y. When y is a named list, list names take precedence. Defaults to sp1, sp2, ....

site_col

Name of the site identifier in the output. Defaults to "site".

season_col

Name of the season identifier in the output. Defaults to "season".

visit_col

Name of the visit identifier. Defaults to "visit".

time_col

Name of the time column in the output. Defaults to "time". The Description gives its values for each layout.

series_col

Name of the species column. Defaults to "series".

y_col

Name of the detection / count column. Defaults to "y". This and the other *_col arguments must each name a different output column.

multi_season

"fused" (the default) or "hierarchical", the layout for data from several seasons. The Description explains both. Data from one season ignore it: a matrix, a [N, J, K] array or a four-dimensional array with \(T = 1\).

Value

A long data.frame with the columns series, site, season, visit, time and y, followed by the covariates. Data from one species have no series column. Data from one season have no season column. Rows where y is NA are dropped. Units may then differ in their number of visits.

See also

occ() and nmix() for the families that take this layout. pivot_species_matrix() converts a site-by-species matrix.

Other model fitting: check_newdata(), jsdgam(), mvgam(), mvgam_data(), mvgam_formula(), mvgam_multiple(), pivot_species_matrix(), series_to_mvgam(), stancode.mvgam_formula(), update.mvgam()

Author

Nicholas J Clark

Examples

# Detections of one species at four sites over three visits, laid out
# as the `y` slot of an unmarked frame. NA marks a missed visit
y <- matrix(c(0, 1, 1,
              0, 0, NA,
              1, 1, 0,
              0, 0, 0), nrow = 4, byrow = TRUE)
long <- pivot_detection_array(
  y,
  site_covs = data.frame(forest = c(0.2, 0.8, 0.5, 0.1)),
  obs_covs = list(wind = matrix(seq(0.1, 1.2, by = 0.1), nrow = 4))
)
# One row per observed visit. The missed visit is dropped
long
#>    site visit time y forest wind
#> 1     1     1    1 0    0.2  0.1
#> 2     1     2    1 1    0.2  0.5
#> 3     1     3    1 1    0.2  0.9
#> 4     2     1    2 0    0.8  0.2
#> 5     2     2    2 0    0.8  0.6
#> 6     3     1    3 1    0.5  0.3
#> 7     3     2    3 1    0.5  0.7
#> 8     3     3    3 0    0.5  1.1
#> 9     4     1    4 0    0.1  0.4
#> 10    4     2    4 0    0.1  0.8
#> 11    4     3    4 0    0.1  1.2

# Three species in a [species, site, visit] array, as spOccupancy
# stores them. Each row names its species in 'series'
set.seed(1)
y3 <- array(rbinom(36, size = 1, prob = 0.4), dim = c(3, 4, 3))
head(pivot_detection_array(y3, species = c("owl", "hawk", "kite")))
#>   series site visit time y
#> 1    owl    1     1    1 0
#> 2    owl    1     2    1 1
#> 3    owl    1     3    1 0
#> 4   hawk    1     1    1 0
#> 5   hawk    1     2    1 0
#> 6   hawk    1     3    1 0

# Next, fit the long frame with mvgam(family = occ())
